summary: H.R. 6422, the American Water Stewardship Act, reauthorizes and updates several Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) water quality protection and restoration programs through fiscal year 2031. It extends funding authorization for programs covering the Great Lakes, Long Island Sound, the Columbia River Basin, the National Estuary Program, and coastal water monitoring. It also adds the Mississippi Sound to the National Estuary Program, modifies eligibility and cost-sharing rules for the San Francisco Bay program, allows beach water grants to be used to identify specific contamination sources, restricts funding to certain foreign entities of concern, and requires a government accountability report on EPA geographic programs.

affected_groups.effect: May receive reauthorized grant funding, become eligible for updated San Francisco Bay grants, and use BEACH Act grants to identify specific contamination sources in coastal waters.
Become eligible for grants provided under the San Francisco Estuary Partnership.
Prohibited from receiving federal funds or participating in projects funded under the specified Clean Water Act programs for fiscal years 2026 through 2031.
affected_groups.group: Non-federal entities connected to foreign countries of concern

key_provisions: Reauthorizes through fiscal year 2031 several water restoration programs, including the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, Long Island Sound Partnership program, Columbia River Basin Restoration Program, National Estuary Program, and BEACH Act program.
Establishes the Mississippi Sound in Mississippi as an estuary of national significance under the National Estuary Program, subject to specific funding conditions for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.

Modifies the San Francisco Estuary Partnership to make federal agencies eligible for grants and sets a maximum federal share of 75 percent for project costs, requiring at least 25 percent from non-federal sources.
Allows state and local governments receiving BEACH Act grants to use funds to identify specific sources of contamination for coastal recreation waters.

Prohibits federal funds made available for fiscal years 2026 through 2031 under specified Clean Water Act programs from going to non-federal entities connected to foreign countries of concern or for projects conducted with them.

Directs the Government Accountability Office to evaluate and report to Congress within two years on specified EPA geographic programs regarding fund management, progress, obstacles, coordination, and ethics policies.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or authorization dollar limits for the reauthorized programs are not mentioned in the source material.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 6422, the American Water Stewardship Act, reauthorizes and updates several Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) water quality protection and restoration programs through fiscal year 2031. It extends funding authorization for programs covering the Great Lakes, Long Island Sound, the Columbia River Basin, the National Estuary Program, and coastal water monitoring. It also adds the Mississippi Sound to the National Estuary Program, modifies eligibility and cost-sharing rules for the San Francisco Bay program, allows beach water grants to be used to identify specific contamination sources, restricts funding to certain foreign entities of concern, and requires a government accountability report on EPA geographic programs.
summary_detail.significance: The bill extends and adjusts major federal water quality and ecosystem restoration programs managed by the EPA through 2031, affects grant distribution rules across multiple states and water basins, introduces foreign entity funding restrictions, and mandates a comprehensive government evaluation of EPA geographic programs.
